observed: §18.3.4 says 'the printed 600 ms' for the 4-bit GGUF tier, but §18.3.2's table prints 800 ms for that row, and §18.3.3 also uses 800 ms ('The 4-bit GGUF tier (800 ms)'). The 600 ms value appears only in §18.8's mini-case, which is a later, explicitly different scenario.
evidence: §18.3.2 table: '70B 4-bit GGUF | $0.15 | 800 | energy only'. §18.3.3: 'The 4-bit GGUF tier (800 ms)'. §18.3.4: '~200× the printed 600 ms'. §18.8: 'Tier 1 (4-bit GGUF): ... latency ~600 ms' and 'the 4-bit tier's ~600 ms latency differs from the ledger's 800 ms'.
root_cause: Forward reference to the mini-case's 600 ms value mislabeled as 'the printed' value; the §18.3.2 ledger prints 800 ms.
correction: Change 'the printed 600 ms' to 'the printed 800 ms' (or 'the mini-case's 600 ms') and recompute the multiple: 117 s / 0.8 s ≈ 146×, not ~200×.
acceptance_test: The multiple in §18.3.4 must match the latency value it cites; if 800 ms is cited, the multiple must be ~146×, not ~200×.

observed: §18.3.1 explicitly concludes that 70B dense 8-bit on 1×H100 holds only ~10 GB KV headroom against the 24.9 GB one canonical 9,500-token request needs — 'zero concurrent canonical requests' — and that the tier 'needs ≥2 GPUs'. The mini-case's Tier 2 runs on 1×H100 without reconciling this.
evidence: §18.3.1: '70B dense 8-bit on 1×H100 holds ~10 GB of KV headroom ... 10/24.89 = 0.40, i.e. zero concurrent canonical requests; the tier needs ≥2 GPUs'. §18.8: 'Tier 2 (70B 8-bit dense): ... Runs on 1×H100.'
root_cause: The mini-case's requests are ~250 tokens (not canonical 9.5K), so 1×H100 is feasible for its short requests — but the mini-case never states this reconciliation, leaving an apparent contradiction with §18.3.1.
correction: Add a sentence to §18.8's Tier 2: 'Unlike the canonical 9.5K case (§18.3.1), these ~250-token requests need only ~0.66 GB KV each, so 1×H100's ~10 GB headroom holds ~15 concurrent requests.'
acceptance_test: The mini-case must explicitly reconcile its 1×H100 placement with §18.3.1's ≥2-GPU finding for canonical requests.

observed: The text says the mixed fleet needs '~18–27 extra hosts' relative to the single-model fleet, but the stated comparison is 58 vs 31, which is exactly 27 extra. The lower bound of 18 is unexplained.
evidence: §18.3.3: 'The mixed fleet needs more hosts than the single-model fleet under the shared placement (58 vs 31 — ~18–27 extra hosts)'.
root_cause: Range likely conflates two different comparisons (58 vs 31 = 27; 58 vs 40 = 18) without stating the second comparison.
correction: Either state the comparison that yields 18 (e.g., '58 vs 40') or replace the range with the single figure '27 extra hosts'.
acceptance_test: The stated range must be derivable from the two host counts given in the same sentence.

quoted_clause: W_reuse(3) ≈ 14.14 s ... ~14.16 s with prefix reuse ... ~14.16 s
observed: The text derives W_reuse(3) ≈ 14.14 s from the stated 100%-prefix-reuse policy (incremental prefix 9,200 + 3×800 = 11,600), but the same section and Table 19-1 print ~14.16 s. The 14.16 value corresponds to using 11,795 (the full retained context) instead of 11,600.
root_cause: Two different prefix-reuse assumptions (11,600 incremental vs 11,795 full retained) are used in different places without reconciliation.
correction: Unify on the stated policy (11,600 incremental prefix) and change all 14.16 values to 14.14, or explicitly state that the table uses the full retained context and change the text's 14.14 to 14.16.
acceptance_test: The W_reuse(3) value must be identical in §19.4 prose, §19.4 summary, and Table 19-1, and must be reproducible from the stated prefix-reuse assumption.

quoted_clause: queue depth 200 × 1 = 200 requests, drained at ~50 rps in ~4 s
observed: The formula in the same sentence says 'buffer depth D·(200−r) requests' = 1 × (200−50) = 150 requests, and 'max queue wait ≈ D·(200−r)/r' = 1 × 150/50 = 3 s. The worked example instead uses 200 requests and ~4 s, which is the total arrivals and total drain time, not the excess buffer and max queue wait.
evidence: §23.8: 'max queue wait ≈ D·(200−r)/r must stay inside the 3 s SLO — so state D, the buffer depth D·(200−r) requests ... worked: D = 1 s at 200 rps → queue depth 200 × 1 = 200 requests, drained at ~50 rps in ~4 s'.
root_cause: Confusion between total arrivals (200) and excess buffer (150), and between total drain time (4 s) and max queue wait (3 s).
correction: Change 'queue depth 200 × 1 = 200 requests, drained at ~50 rps in ~4 s' to 'buffer depth 1 × (200−50) = 150 requests, drained at ~50 rps in ~3 s'.
acceptance_test: The worked example's buffer depth and drain time must match the formula D·(200−r) and D·(200−r)/r stated in the same sentence.
